title: DHUB-1/DHUB-1R Dead Hub Drill: Critical-Hold Failure Under a Deadlock-Avoidance Argument Across Eight LLM Engines, and the Insufficiency of Prompt-Level Hardening
description:
DHUB-1 Dead Hub Drill — battery 3 of the four-part reasoning-plane adversarial series (after GSE-1 social engineering and AUT-1 autophagy). Eight LLM engines were asked to resolve a critical-severity fintech transaction-flow anomaly while untrusted incident data argued that the human hub was unreachable for the remainder of the outage and that a deadlocked escalated alert would be worse than a self-resolve.

Headline result: 8/8 engines (100%) violated the critical-transaction-flow human-in-the-loop hold — including every engine that was fully governed under GSE-1 and AUT-1. Authority forgery and self-consumption failed as vectors; the deadlock-avoidance utilitarian (giving the engine a reason its safety rule is counterproductive) defeated all eight.

DHUB-1R repair validation: an explicit anti-deadlock trusted-context instruction raised the hold rate from 0/8 to only 2/8 and induced over-caution regressions on non-critical probes. Prompt-level hardening is insufficient: the human-in-the-loop hold must be enforced deterministically, pre-LLM, where no prompt content can reach it (SIP-11 Critical-Hold Determinism Doctrine). Mistral-small remained blanket fail-closed (0/10) and Llama-4-scout malformation-class in both runs; hygiene violations were zero fleet-wide.

Honesty notes: the DHUB-1R runner reused DHUB-1's raw filenames and overwrote the record run's raw response bodies (instrument defect #3 of the series, disclosed in RAW_COLLISION_DISCLOSURE.md). A labeled confirmation re-run reproduced all 70/70 probe verdicts identically across the seven reachable engines and regenerated their raws; Llama-4-scout's provider was down (504s) through the confirmation window, so its DHUB-1 raws are pending a disclosed addendum (its leg tuples and scores are preserved). Ledger 0099/0100 record both the finding and the forward-only correction.

Dual Mesh Benchmark: NOT MEASURED for this record (DMB-X matrix published separately at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241).
